recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is. It completes the FHIR-17172 host requirement without broadening the regex or deciding separate historical questions about anchoring and other URL grammar details.
issue_request: FHIR-17172 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and reported that http://Patient/1 was invalid but passed the REST URL regex; the accepted resolution said a scheme requires a host, while http://example.com////////Patient/1 remains valid.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by svn revision 14232, represented in git by 075cd55564e68888a3325e4c90f920d74aa5fe53, changing the optional absolute URL prefix from zero-or-more slash-delimited segments to one-or-more. A same-day FHIR-14079 follow-up added '-' to the character class. The current source still allowed an empty first segment such as http:///Patient/1 because the repeated segment itself allowed zero characters.
additional_context: source/references.html is the active References page source for this regex and is referenced by other current source such as Bundle.fullUrl guidance. Later Published issue FHIR-34405 only added an optional fragment suffix and cautionary prose, and searches of Zulip and Confluence found no conflicting community decision.
reconciliation: Changed the optional absolute RESTful prefix from one-or-more possibly empty segments to one required non-empty first segment followed by zero-or-more possibly empty later segments. This preserves relative references and hosted absolute references, including repeated slashes after a host, while rejecting empty-host absolute URLs.
source_changes: source/references.html: updated the RESTful-reference regex prefix to require at least one allowed character before the first slash after http:// or https://, while allowing subsequent empty slash-delimited segments.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published issue for the same References-page regex; its hyphen allowance is preserved, but its separate anchoring wording was not decided here.
Later Published issue appended the optional fragment suffix to the same regex and did not change the scheme/host rule.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive STU3 issue reported that http://Patient/1 was invalid but passed the REST URL regex, and resolved that a scheme requires a host while repeated slashes after a host are valid.
evidence_items.learned: The regex should require a non-empty host segment whenever an http or https scheme is present.

evidence_items.summary: The active References page source contains the RESTful-reference regex shown to implementers.

evidence_items.summary: The original application changed the URL-prefix segment repetition from * to +, and the same-day follow-up added '-' to the character class.
evidence_items.learned: The exact reported http://Patient/1 case was addressed, but the current repeated empty segment form still allowed an empty authority such as http:///Patient/1.

evidence_items.summary: Later Published issue FHIR-34405 appended an optional fragment suffix to the same regex and added cautionary prose.
evidence_items.learned: Later history did not supersede or loosen FHIR-17172's requirement for a host when a scheme is present.
